title: Online Clothes Shopping — Promotional Purchase
goal: Customer finds, purchases, receives, and either keeps or returns a clothing item bought through a promotional offer
summary: A universal service mission capturing the end-to-end experience of promotional-triggered online clothes shopping. The graph covers discovery through notification, browsing and selection, purchase, delivery, try-on, and resolution (keep or return). Multiple personas can flow through this mission, each generating their own Experience artifact.

scope.trigger: Promotional push notification from shopping app
scope.completion: Item kept and worn, OR refund received after return

laneContent.description: Customer receives a push notification about a flash sale from the shopping app
designOpportunities: Personalize notification based on browsing history
Include specific product recommendations

significance.description: First contact point — notification timing and relevance determines engagement

laneContent.description: Customer taps notification and lands on the sale landing page

barriers.description: App takes 8 seconds to fully load sale page

designOpportunities: Pre-cache sale content before notification send
Show countdown timer for urgency

laneContent.description: Customer browses sale categories, applies filters (size, price, category), scrolls through products

barriers.description: Difficult to assess fabric quality from photos alone
Filter options reset when navigating back from product detail

designOpportunities: Persist filter selections throughout session
Show fabric detail close-ups automatically

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: Familiarity with clothing sizes and filter/sort UI patterns
cognitive.supportAvailable: Filter labels and category headings; no contextual help or guidance tooltips present

laneContent.description: Customer selects a product and views details: images, price, description, sale discount
designOpportunities: Show 'you saved £X' prominently
Suggest styling options or accessories

significance.description: Key conversion point — product detail must build purchase intent

laneContent.description: Customer consults the size guide to determine correct size

barriers.description: Size guide shows measurements but no guidance on fit style (relaxed vs fitted)
No information about model's size for reference

designOpportunities: Add model size and height information
Include fit predictor based on previous purchases
Show customer photos with size information

cognitive.priorKnowledgeRequired: Understanding of body measurements (cm/inches), knowledge of how fit styles (relaxed, regular, fitted) differ across brands
cognitive.supportAvailable: Measurement table only; no fit-style guidance, no comparison to previously purchased items, no contextual help

laneContent.description: Customer reads reviews, filters by photo reviews, looks for sizing feedback

barriers.description: Cannot verify if reviews are genuine

designOpportunities: Aggregate sizing feedback into a simple indicator
Allow filtering reviews by reviewer body type
Highlight verified purchase reviews

significance.description: Trust-building point — review quality directly affects purchase confidence

laneContent.description: Customer navigates to return policy to understand conditions and process

barriers.description: Return policy requires navigating away from product page

designOpportunities: Show return policy summary directly on product page
Badge products with 'Free Returns' prominently

laneContent.description: Customer decides whether the item is worth purchasing given price, reviews, sizing confidence, and return policy
Customer selects size, adds item to cart
Customer reviews cart contents, verifies pricing, checks delivery threshold

barriers.description: Promotional upsell suggestions add friction to checkout flow

laneContent.description: Customer confirms delivery address, selects delivery method, reviews delivery estimate
designOpportunities: Show specific delivery date rather than range where possible
laneContent.frontstage: Saved address auto-populated, delivery options with estimated dates and costs, order summary sidebar
laneContent.backstage: Address validation service checks postcode. Carrier API queries real-time delivery slots. Inventory system confirms stock reservation.

sla.escalation: Flag for UX review if median session duration exceeds target; trigger A/B test on checkout form simplification

laneContent.description: Customer selects payment method and authenticates
laneContent.frontstage: Saved payment methods displayed, Apple Pay / Google Pay biometric prompt, processing animation
laneContent.backstage: Payment gateway sends authorisation request. Fraud engine scores transaction. On approval: inventory hard-reserved, order record created, confirmation email queued.
data-required: Payment token (from Apple Pay / saved card)
Fraud score inputs (device ID, IP, purchase history)

sla.escalation: Alert payments operations team; surface customer support contact if authorisation takes over 30 seconds

laneContent.description: System confirms order and sends confirmation email with order number
designOpportunities: Include styling tips in confirmation
Offer calendar reminder for delivery

significance.description: Commitment point — order is placed, customer enters waiting period

laneContent.description: System notifies customer that order has shipped with tracking information
Customer can check tracking status. Package moves through courier network.

barriers.description: Tracking updates are generic and don't give specific delivery time

designOpportunities: Provide delivery time window on day of delivery
Allow scheduling specific delivery time

laneContent.description: Package is delivered. Customer retrieves, opens, and inspects the item.
designOpportunities: Include styling card or lookbook
Add QR code linking to styling videos

significance.description: First physical interaction with the product — expectations meet reality

laneContent.description: Customer tries on the clothing item and evaluates fit, quality, and appearance

barriers.description: Online sizing information often doesn't predict fit for individual body types

designOpportunities: Offer virtual try-on technology
Provide body-shape specific recommendations
Better sizing prediction based on purchase/return history

significance.description: Critical moment of truth — determines keep or return

laneContent.description: Customer decides whether the item fits well enough to keep or needs to be returned
Customer removes tags and integrates the item into their wardrobe
Customer opens the app, navigates to order, selects return, provides reason

barriers.description: Required to provide detailed reason for return

designOpportunities: Use return reasons to improve sizing recommendations
Offer style consultation for future purchases

laneContent.description: Customer chooses between return methods (Post Office, Locker, Home collection) and receives return label/QR code
designOpportunities: Pre-select nearest return location
Show wait time estimates for different methods

laneContent.description: Customer repackages the item for return shipment
designOpportunities: Provide reusable return packaging with original shipment
Include clear repackaging instructions

laneContent.description: Customer drops off packaged return at selected location (locker, post office, etc.)
designOpportunities: Provide estimated refund date at drop-off
Offer instant refund for trusted customers

laneContent.description: System confirms return has been received and refund is processing

barriers.description: No specific timeframe given for refund processing

designOpportunities: Provide specific refund date estimate
Show refund progress tracker

laneContent.description: Refund is processed and customer receives confirmation
designOpportunities: Include personalized recommendations in refund confirmation
Offer incentive for next purchase

significance.description: Closing the loop — refund experience determines future purchase confidence

condition.description: Item fits well and meets expectations
Item doesn't fit or doesn't meet expectations

paths.name: Happy path (item fits)
paths.description: Customer purchases and keeps the item

paths.name: Return path (item doesn't fit)
paths.description: Customer purchases, tries on, and returns the item

paths.name: Browse abandonment
paths.description: Customer browses but nothing compels purchase

phases.name: Discovery
phases.goal: Become aware of a compelling offer
